release: 2025 BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey; released October 29, 2026
measurement: U.S. mean annual spending per consumer unit (not median bills, not cost of identical goods). Monthly figures are annual/12, rounded for display.
integrity: 2025 survey uses BLS weighting to adjust for October-November 2025 data collection interruption. Source table may revise the 2024 comparison. Headline categories can overlap with subcategories; never sum across issue cards.

housing.title: Housing
housing.intro: The national housing figure includes shelter, utilities and other household costs; it is not a typical local rent or mortgage payment.
housing.localNote: Area median gross rent from the 2020–2024 ACS is a distinct measure of renter-occupied homes—not comparable dollar-for-dollar with the national total housing spending average.

drivers.label: Housing supply and location
drivers.why: The number and types of available homes, access to jobs and land-use rules change market competition for space.
drivers.who: Local planning bodies, landowners, developers and landlords
drivers.choice: Check proposed zoning changes and compare equivalent local units.

drivers.label: Financing and rent terms
drivers.why: Mortgage interest rates, credit terms, lease renewals and property carrying costs change what residents must pay.
drivers.who: Lenders, property owners, monetary policy and consumer protection agencies
drivers.choice: Compare full borrowing cost or lease terms, not only the advertised monthly rate.

drivers.label: Utilities and maintenance
drivers.why: Energy, insurance, taxes, repairs and building operations can raise housing outlays even without an increase in base rent.
drivers.who: Utilities, insurers, contractors and property-tax authorities
drivers.choice: Separate contract charges from usage and look for eligible relief or competition.

housing.disclaimer: The breakdown describes average spending categories, not the share of price inflation caused by each actor.

groceries.title: Groceries

headline.label: Food purchased to eat at home

groceries.intro: This is grocery spending, not restaurant or takeout spending, and not the price of a fixed basket. In 2025 the BLS average rose 4.3%—a spending change, not a grocery price inflation rate.
groceries.localNote: No validated store-by-store, unit-price basket is linked to this ZIP. Census measures of food assistance are not grocery-price measurements.

drivers.label: Farming and processing
drivers.why: Crop yields, livestock costs, food processing and packaging determine part of the cost before products reach shelves.
drivers.who: Agricultural producers, food processors and food brands
drivers.choice: Compare seasonal choices and comparable products by unit price.

drivers.label: Distribution and competition
drivers.why: Freight, storage, local store access and the number of competitive retailers affect the choices and prices shoppers face.
drivers.who: Retail chains, wholesalers, logistics firms and competition regulators
drivers.choice: Compare real nearby stores, including travel and delivery costs.

drivers.label: Brand, package and promotion
drivers.why: Advertising, branded premiums, package size and promotions change how much usable food a dollar buys.
drivers.who: Food manufacturers and retailers
drivers.choice: Compare price per usable ounce or serving; promotions are not always better deals.

groceries.disclaimer: Spending changes can reflect quantities and product choices as well as prices. Ownership links alone do not prove price effects.

energy.title: Utilities
energy.intro: This national broad utilities line includes more than energy. It is already part of the BLS housing category, so never add it again to housing.

secondary.label: 2025 U.S. residential electricity price
secondary.definition: U.S. average residential retail price per kilowatt-hour; not an electricity bill, local tariff or energy budget.

energy.localNote: ZIP alone cannot identify a specific utility provider, plan, meter or 2026 retail tariff. Existing state all-sector electricity data are from 2024 and are not a direct residential comparison.

drivers.label: Fuel and power generation
drivers.why: Power plant fuels, generation mix and wholesale supply costs change production costs.
drivers.who: Electric utilities, generators, fuel suppliers and regulators
drivers.choice: Check utility-provided breakdowns of supply and delivery charges.

drivers.label: Grid and infrastructure
drivers.why: Transmission, distribution, reliability and weather-related system investments affect delivery costs and approved rates.
drivers.who: Utilities, state utility commissions and grid operators
drivers.choice: Check published rate cases and assistance or efficiency programs.

drivers.label: How much is used
drivers.why: Household heating or cooling needs, building efficiency and rate plans affect the consumption portion of bills.
drivers.who: Households, property owners, utility providers
drivers.choice: Use actual bill kWh/therms to compare usage, fees and eligible plans.

energy.disclaimer: National utilities spending is already included in the housing total; no double-counting or conversion from cents/kWh to a bill without usage data.

health.title: Healthcare
health.intro: Insurance spending dominates this average. It includes premiums and direct purchases; it is not the total amount paid to providers by all insurers or government programs.
health.localNote: Area uninsured rates from ACS are coverage statistics, not local premiums or patient charges.

drivers.label: Insurance plan design
drivers.why: Premiums, deductibles, co-payments, provider networks and subsidies can shift what patients pay out of pocket.
drivers.who: Insurers, employers and state/federal regulators
drivers.choice: Compare annual premiums plus expected out-of-pocket costs and network access.

drivers.label: Provider and treatment prices
drivers.why: Negotiated rates, regional provider supply and the service selected can change patient bills.
drivers.who: Hospitals, physicians, insurers and public programs
drivers.choice: Check covered networks and published price estimates before elective services.

drivers.label: Medicines and formularies
drivers.why: Manufacturer pricing, pharmacy contracting, formularies and copay tiers influence prescription payments.
drivers.who: Manufacturers, pharmacy benefit managers, pharmacies and health plans
drivers.choice: Review plan coverage with a pharmacist or prescriber before changing treatment.

health.disclaimer: A national mean is not a medical recommendation or a price quote for any health plan.

work.title: Jobs & pay
work.intro: This measures average consumer-unit income, not individual wages or the 'cost of a job'. Nearby ACS median household income is a different statistic.
work.localNote: 2020–2024 ACS median household income is a local median, not directly equivalent to 2025 national average income before taxes.

drivers.label: Local industry and demand
drivers.why: Occupation mix, employer openings and industry demand shape available pay and opportunity.
drivers.who: Businesses, local economic development officials and employers
drivers.choice: Compare same-job wages from published local occupation tables.

drivers.label: Bargaining and labor rules
drivers.why: Wage floors, benefit design, contracts and negotiating power can affect take-home compensation.
drivers.who: Employers, workers and legislators
drivers.choice: Check wage rights, worker protections and comparable compensation.

drivers.label: Work-linked expenses
drivers.why: Commute, childcare, mandatory fees and scheduling can reduce the net value of a job.
drivers.who: Employers, service providers, transit agencies and regulators
drivers.choice: Compare net compensation after required expenses, not salary alone.

work.disclaimer: Income changes do not measure changes in purchasing power without price and household-composition adjustment.

schools.title: Schools & children
schools.intro: The CE education figure is not a local tuition quote, a school budget, or a universal childcare cost. Many families have no education outlay while others pay far more.
schools.localNote: Local preschool enrollment counts and school spending per pupil are not tuition rates or childcare fees; district assignment requires an actual address.

drivers.label: Childcare labor and availability
drivers.why: Staffing levels, caregiver wages, group size and limited slots can change private care fees.
drivers.who: Care providers, state licensing agencies and local governments
drivers.choice: Compare equivalent licensed programs and check assistance eligibility.

drivers.label: Public school funding
drivers.why: State formulas, property taxes, grants and district budgets influence program resources.
drivers.who: Legislators, school boards and administrators
drivers.choice: Read your district budget and published school profiles.

drivers.label: Extra services
drivers.why: After-school care, transportation, tutoring and activities can create additional household costs.
drivers.who: School districts, contractors and community programs
drivers.choice: Check public, library and community alternatives, with hours and suitability.

schools.disclaimer: Do not interpret the $1,583 national education average as an early childcare or per-child school expense.

transport.title: Getting around
transport.intro: Transportation costs are route specific: subway and commuter rail fares, tolls (which may apply only one way), congestion charges, parking and fuel can all be paid on the same trip. The national spending total is not a typical commute price.
transport.localNote: A ZIP-area commute mode share does not reveal actual tolls, fare zones, passes or travel routes. Source-backed regional examples are selectable; there is no automatic route or price inference.

drivers.label: Vehicle prices and finance
drivers.why: Manufacturer prices, financing rates and purchase choices change the biggest vehicle-related outlay.
drivers.who: Manufacturers, lenders, dealers and consumers
drivers.choice: Compare full contract and ownership costs rather than monthly payments.

drivers.label: Fuel and maintenance
drivers.why: Fuel markets, insurance, vehicle reliability and repair labor affect recurring operating costs.
drivers.who: Energy firms, insurers, repair providers and regulators
drivers.choice: Compare coverage and service quotes; measure actual mileage and maintenance needs.

drivers.label: Transit access and public investment
drivers.why: Service frequency, fare policies, route coverage and public subsidies determine whether transit is a workable substitute.
drivers.who: Transit agencies, elected budget authorities and operators
drivers.choice: Compare available routes, passes and time reliability before deciding.

drivers.label: Tolls, subway fares and transportation policy
drivers.why: Public authorities approve fares and tolls using published budgets, service obligations, debt and capital plans. Different agencies charge separately and transfer, payment-method and discount rules determine what riders actually pay.
drivers.who: Transit boards, bridge/tunnel authorities, public finance officials, elected lawmakers and commuters
drivers.choice: Check each published fare and toll, charged direction and eligibility for caps, passes or credits, then compare all-in travel choices.

drivers.label: Procurement waste, vendor influence and corruption oversight
drivers.why: Weak contract controls, conflicts or corruption can increase public project and operating expenses. An auditor finding, prosecution or donation does not itself establish that any particular fare or toll increase was caused by the problem.
drivers.who: Transit procurement teams, contractors, investors, inspectors general, regulators and boards
drivers.choice: Trace audited contract payments, procurement decisions, public oversight findings and the rate-setting budget before assigning cost responsibility.

transport.disclaimer: National BLS transportation expenses combine cars and transit, but do not identify the cost of a specific commuting route. Transit charges, tolls and corruption cases are sourced separately; neither contract waste nor a political relationship is equated with a household price increase without documented causation.

public-services.title: Taxes & local services
public-services.intro: No one national monthly amount correctly describes a household's taxes or the services that household receives. Spending surveys and government budgets answer different questions.
public-services.localNote: ZIP codes cross taxing and school-district boundaries. Verified personal tax burdens need parcel, income and jurisdiction-specific rules.

drivers.label: Income and sales tax rules
drivers.why: Tax bases, progressive brackets, exclusions and local rates determine tax liabilities.
drivers.who: Congress, state legislatures, tax agencies and local governments
drivers.choice: Use official schedules and check only the credits or exemptions that apply.

drivers.label: Property assessment and spending
drivers.why: Taxable assessments, local budgets and overlapping jurisdictions help set property-tax bills.
drivers.who: Local assessors, school boards and councils
drivers.choice: Verify actual taxing entities and appeal or exemption rules.

drivers.label: Service fees and infrastructure
drivers.why: Water, sanitation, permits and other services rely on local contracts, operating costs and capital work.
drivers.who: Local utilities, public works and contractors
drivers.choice: Review original budgets and fees; compare service quality alongside cost.

public-services.disclaimer: This is a decision and funding map, not a computed personal tax bill.

representation.title: Your voice
representation.intro: Political influence has documented relationships, but it has no universal monthly price tag. Trace funding, public decisions and verified downstream measures separately.
representation.localNote: A ZIP code is not a verified election-district boundary or evidence of personal political identity.

drivers.label: Campaign finance disclosure
drivers.why: Public filings document donors, recipients and expenditures; they do not by themselves demonstrate a vote was bought.
drivers.who: Candidates, committees and the Federal Election Commission
drivers.choice: Inspect committee records and their reporting dates.

drivers.label: Rules and oversight
drivers.why: Legislation, agency enforcement and judicial decisions can shape markets and public services.
drivers.who: Legislators, agencies, courts and state institutions
drivers.choice: Open the original bill, ruling or enforcement record.

drivers.label: Local decisions
drivers.why: Zoning, transit, tax and utility governance affect daily life through different jurisdictional structures.
drivers.who: Local elected bodies and administrative authorities
drivers.choice: Check official local hearings and comment opportunities.

representation.disclaimer: No direct cause or household cost is attributed to a politician or donor without specific validated evidence.
